The role of the nurses, midwives and the interprofessional team will be considered in view of caring for the patient as they are supported through the journey. Using case-based learning and the clinical reasoning cycle you will reflect on your own values about health, illness, dying and death. This will give you the opportunity to explore a person and family-centred approach to pain, oncology, palliative and end of life care.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of legal and ethical considerations to advanced care planning, advocacy and guardianship for persons experiencing pain, palliative and oncological needs.
Describe the pathophysiology related to pain, oncology treatment and palliative conditions.
Discuss a range of therapies and evidence-based nursing practice in the management of pain, oncology, palliative and end of life care treatment.
Discuss the mental health considerations when providing care for individuals experiencing pain and receiving oncology treatment, palliative or end of life care
Critically apply the key principles, philosophies and approaches that underpin the care of patients requiring acute or persistent pain management, oncology treatment, palliative and end of life care.
Critically examine and reflect on the role of nurses and midwives as part of the interprofessional team in pain management, oncology, palliative and end of life care.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Patient care plan and reflection (4,000 words)

workload_hours: 12 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials, simulations and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Safety and quality in ageing and chronic conditions
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit focuses on the essential requirements you will need to understand patient safety, quality care and risk management. There is a focus on the care of the older person and those with chronic conditions, including for priority populations. You will explore collaboration with the interprofessional team to enable safe and quality care of the older person and those with chronic conditions. You will examine the nursing and midwifery role in healthcare access, equity and service navigation for those from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, priority populations and those with chronic conditions. Strength-based and socially inclusive approaches for safe and quality nursing and midwifery practice and skills are emphasised.
learning_outcomes: Discuss safety, quality and risk in older people and those living with chronic conditions.

Analyse the nursing role in healthcare access, equity and service navigation for those from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, priority populations and those living with chronic conditions.
Evaluate how the interprofessional teams collaborate to provide safe, quality care.
Articulate risk-management principles to promote a culture of safety in the provision of care.
Examine principles of governance, safety and quality in health.
Explore the impact of cognitive impairment on individuals, families and carers.
Examine psycho-social factors affecting older people and those living with chronic conditions.
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials, interprofessional learning, online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Leadership, education and quality improvement in nursing practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit builds on the concepts covered in the core units in years one (1), two (2) and three (3). You will explore education, quality improvement and leadership, which are critical in addressing complex healthcare issues. To strengthen lifelong learning, you will explore and apply teaching and learning theories to provide education to your patients and your peers. You will build knowledge and skills about your role in quality improvement in healthcare. You will demonstrate effective leadership skills to role model the delivery of evidence-based practice in complex health care systems.
learning_outcomes: Appraise leadership theories that enable person-centred care.
Discuss the nursing role in leading quality improvement.
Plan, design and deliver tailored and evidence-based educational experiences.
Analyse evidence-based policies, guidelines and standards to support safe nursing practice.
Examine teaching and learning theories for patient and professional education.
Discuss the impact of leadership on improving healthcare delivery.
Explore quality improvement for innovation in healthcare.
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials, teaching session and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Translation of nursing knowledge to complex acute care practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: The unit will provide you the opportunity for integration of advanced health assessment skills, and application of evidence-based practice and ethical principles in the management of complex nursing situations in simulated and actual clinical settings. You will be introduced to the nursing management of patients with complex and/or life threatening health problems. Pathophysiology, pharmacology, and healthcare interventions will be critically evaluated in the context of complex healthcare issues. You will develop clinical judgement skills through the translation of knowledge involving the management of the deteriorating patient.
learning_outcomes: Explain use of appropriate therapeutic medications in the patient with complex and/or life threatening illness
Identify, analyse and resolve clinical concerns in the patient with complex and/or life threatening illness
Apply pathophysiological concepts to patients with complex and/or life threatening illness
Undertake complex nursing activities in a range of health settings, and apply appropriate principles of prioritising and time management appropriate to the clinical setting

Practice with increasing independence in accordance with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) Professional Standards for the Registered Nurse, Code of ethics and Code of professional conduct for nurses
Identify and implement response systems for the deteriorating patient in the clinical setting
Develop and implement patient-centred care appropriate to the diverse needs and wishes of the patient and their family/carer
Critically evaluate judgements made in the performance of informed patient care

assessment_tasks.task_name: Case study analysis and reflection (3,000 words)
Final scheduled assessment (exam) (2 hours and 30 minutes)

workload_hours: 8 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials, clinical learning environment and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Clinical honours thesis 1: Applied research methods and skills
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit provides you with the opportunity to encounter a challenging research environment through the interaction of philosophical paradigms and extension of theoretical knowledge and acquisitions of skills to facilitate the undertaking of a research project. The unit will build upon knowledge gained in core undergraduate research units. You will be allocated a research supervisor to begin formulating research questions and methodology for subsequent study.
learning_outcomes: Develop and utilise research skills in the following areas: + advanced online searching; + documentation management; + data collection methods and analysis; and
Begin formulating research question and proposed study.
Evaluate and utilise appropriate philosophical foundations of research;
Distinguish and critique quantitative and qualitative methodologies;
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Clinical honours thesis 2: Framing a research proposal
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: The unit provides you with the opportunity to develop an appropriate hypothesis or research question and derive an appropriate research design showing regard to the practical problems of conducting research in nursing or midwifery settings. Ethical issues in research are also considered. You will develop your own research proposal and seek ethical approval to conduct your study under the supervision of an academic staff member.
learning_outcomes: Identify issues related to the conduct of the proposed research;
Identify a research topic that addresses a significant nursing or midwifery issue;
Participate in research seminars and workshops;
Develop a research problem, question or hypothesis;
Describe the theoretical basis behind the topic and research design;
Demonstrate a collaborative and critical approach to research.
Apply to ethics committees for research approval as necessary; and
Formulate and present a research plan;
Develop and present a research proposal, including a literature review;
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Translation of nursing knowledge in preparation for professional practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit builds on NUR3310, supporting students to develop nursing management skills related to the deteriorating patient in acute settings, and NUR2225 related to the client with an escalating mental health condition. The unit focuses on teamwork, resilience, clinical risk and professional identity to prepare students for transition to professional practice. This approach will complement the extensive clinical experience that students will undertake during this unit. In simulated and clinical settings, students will apply evidence-based diagnostic, therapeutic and preventative techniques associated with caring for patients with complex healthcare needs in a range of healthcare settings.
learning_outcomes: Apply the principles of clinical risk and patient safety in a variety of healthcare settings.
Demonstrate a person-centred approach to assessing, planning, implementing and evaluating care and outcomes through the life-span across all healthcare settings.
Identify and discuss strategies to manage the challenges of contemporary nursing and midwifery practice.
Identify and develop strategies for personal and professional resilience.
Apply evidence-based diagnostic, therapeutic and preventative techniques associated with caring for patients with complex health-care needs.
Apply time management and problem solving skills in the delivery of patient care.
Identify strategies to engage in ongoing professional role development for nurses and midwives.
Demonstrate effective communication within an inter-professional team to deliver quality patient care.
Recognise and respond to the deteriorating patient.
Evaluate leadership, management, teamwork and inter-professional collaboration in the provision of quality patient care.
prerequisites: NUR3310: Translation of nursing knowledge to complex acute care practice
workload_hours: 7 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including simulation tutorials, clinical learning environment and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Clinical honours thesis 3: Conducting a research project
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: The unit provides you with the opportunity to implement the research proposal developed in NUR4402. You will further develop a literature review, finalise ethical approval for their research, and collect, organise and manage the data for the study. With your research supervisors, you will explore a range of issues that can arise during the research process.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate effective progress towards research plan;
Finalise the ethics approval process for the project;
Discuss issues arising during the research process;
Work collaboratively with a research supervisor to achieve research milestones (e.g. submission of ethics proposal);
Present research findings in a seminar context.
Demonstrate an awareness of ethical and privacy issues as they apply to their research proposal;
Generate a critical review of the literature and theoretical frameworks relevant to their field of study;
Accurately collect, manage and secure data for research activities;
Write to an academic standard by incorporating existing research findings and supervisor feedback; and
Respond appropriately to the realities of research project issues including identification of a research site (or sites) and recruitment of participants;
Undertake data collection both accurately and ethically;
Conduct a pilot study (if appropriate) to anticipate and address practical problems that may arise in the course of data collection;
prerequisites: NUR4401: Clinical honours thesis 1: Applied research methods and skills
NUR4402: Clinical honours thesis 2: Framing a research proposal
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Clinical honours thesis 4: Analysing and reporting research
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: The unit provides you with the opportunity to develop appropriate research knowledge and skills as you, with the assistance of a supervisor, analyse and interpret the data collected in Clinical Honours Thesis III. Following this, the research will be written in the form of a literature review and article suitable for publication, and be presented at a research seminar. The clinical/midwifery practice in this unit will allow the you to exit the program at the level of an advanced novice practitioner.
learning_outcomes: Write to an appropriate academic standard by incorporating existing research findings and supervisor feedback;
Respond appropriately to realities of research project issues (e.g. ethical and practical issues surrounding confidentiality, data management etc.);
Generate a report on the project, demonstrating critical analysis and discussion of findings in the context of prior research showing due regard to relevant stylistic conventions;
Work collaboratively with a research supervisor to achieve research milestones;
Identify strengths and limitations in their research design;
Address practicalities of research project management.
Demonstrate an ability to manage data collection and analysis;
Conduct appropriate data analysis and interpretation;
Suggest directions for future research in their specialist area; and
Analyse and present data in a clear, concise and systematic manner;
Present research findings in a seminar context;
prerequisites: NUR4402: Clinical honours thesis 2: Framing a research proposal
NUR4403: Clinical honours thesis 3: Conducting a research project
NUR4401: Clinical honours thesis 1: Applied research methods and skills
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Mental health nursing in contemporary practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit builds on concepts learned in Contemporary Nursing Practice 1 and 2, and will introduce new knowledge for developing your clinical nursing skills when working with people experiencing mental health conditions. People experiencing mental health conditions can present to any healthcare setting, therefore nurses require the skills to engage in meaningful therapeutic relationships to work effectively with people with a mental health condition, carers, families and their supporters. You will develop therapeutic skills to support holistic assessment and identify appropriate interventions used in providing person-centred and recovery focused care to promote positive outcomes for service users. Clinical placement will provide you with the opportunity for translation of theory to the clinical practice environment.
learning_outcomes: Plan and prioritise person-centred nursing interventions for people who are experiencing mental health conditions.

Demonstrate practice at a beginning level in accordance with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) Registered nurse standards for practice, Code of conduct for nurses and the International Council of Nurses (ICN) Code of ethics for nurses.
Apply relevant mental health legislation when caring for people with mental health conditions.
Identify and explain the communication skills and qualities required to develop and maintain a therapeutic relationship
Examine factors that impact a person’s mental health and identify barriers to receiving care.
prerequisites: NUR5007: Primary and global health in contemporary nursing practice

assessment_tasks.task_name: Final scheduled assessment (2 hours and 10 minutes)

workload_hours: 8 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials, simulation tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Contemporary nursing practice 2
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this clinically focussed medical-surgical nursing practice unit, you will build upon the concepts introduced in NUR5111 Contemporary Nursing Practice 1. You will explore pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, pharmacology, associated microbiology and nursing care associated with a range of common health conditions. The clinical practice component will provide you with opportunities to incorporate your theoretical learning into clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate practice at a beginning level in accordance with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) Registered nurse standards for practice, Code of conduct for nurses and the International Council of Nurses (ICN) Code of ethics for nurses.
Apply knowledge of the pathophysiology of common conditions to the nursing care of clients in medical-surgical settings.
Describe the nursing application of diagnostic, therapeutic and preventative techniques associated with caring for the medical-surgical patient.
Critically reflect upon, and evaluate self-performance in terms of the delivery of quality nursing care.
Apply pharmacological knowledge to support the safe medication management of patients with an acute illness.
Demonstrate safe, evidence based and person-centred clinical nursing practice relevant to medical-surgical setting.
Demonstrate in-depth knowledge of common health problems for the patient in the acute medical-surgical setting.

Develop and implement patient centred nursing care appropriate to the needs and wishes of the patient and their family/carer, regardless of race, age, gender, culture, sexual orientation, disability or other diverse needs.
workload_hours: 9 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials, clinical learning environments and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Foundations of professional nursing practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit will introduce you to the foundational professional skills essential for nursing practice. You will examine nursing from a socio-political framework and will be introduced to professional standards and ethical codes that underpin nursing practice. You will explore legal and ethical theories and principles that relate to nursing practice in the Australian healthcare context.
learning_outcomes: Apply ethical theories and principles to inform decision-making in clinical practice.
Apply the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) Standards and Codes of practice that underpin the expected behaviour and attitudes of registered nurses in Australia.
Analyse the legal implications of actions taken in nursing practice.
Explore the socio-political factors that influence nursing practice in the Australian healthcare context.
workload_hours: 12 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Contemporary nursing practice 4
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit focuses on preparing you for the transition to practice as a Registered Nurse. In preparing for this transition to health professional, you will explore: the integration of advanced health assessment skills, the clinical application of evidence-based practice, the management of complex nursing situations, inter and intra-professional practice, resilience and self-management.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on actions, professional development and on the nature of nursing practice in relation to the nursing management of clients' health needs
Collaborate within an interprofessional team in the provision of quality care
Undertake complex nursing activities in a range of clinical settings and effectively apply prioritising, problem solving and time management skills
Apply knowledge of appropriate therapeutic medications in the care of patients with complex or life-threatening illnesses

Demonstrate practice at a beginning level in accordance with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) Registered Nurse Standards for Practice , Code of conduct for nurses and the International Council of Nurses (ICN) Code of ethics for nurses
Support near peers in a range of skills relating to patient assessment and care within a clinical setting
Reflect on and evaluate performance of self and others related to knowledge, skills and delivery of nursing care
Demonstrate clinical judgement skills to identify, analyse and resolve clinical concerns in the patient with complex and/or life threatening illnesses
Demonstrate a systematic approach to identify, assess and respond to the deteriorating patient
Critically reflect on specific learning needs in preparation for registration as a nurse
workload_hours: 9 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials, clinical learning environments and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Primary and global health in contemporary nursing practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this unit you will explore the key principles and concepts of health that inform the frameworks guiding disease prevention. You will develop an understanding of: health and illness; global and population health; social determinants of health, environmental impacts on health; therapeutic communication and cultural safety; health promotion and health screening. This will provide a foundation for you to explore and reflect on the provision of health care to underserved populations and nursing in a culturally diverse community.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the impact of globalisation on human health, considering social, economic, and political factors.
Analyse the factors contributing to health inequities for priority populations, and evaluate strategies to improve access to healthcare and equitable service provision.

Demonstrate practice at a beginning level in accordance with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) Registered nurse standards for practice, Code of conduct for nurses and the International Council of Nurses Code of Ethics for Nurses.
Critically evaluate the concepts of planetary, global, and public health and their impact on nursing practice.
Apply evidence-based research and show how planetary, global and public health impact healthcare delivery.
Evaluate the influence of the social determinants of health, and review global and local strategies to improve health and equity outcomes.
Critically evaluate and appraise the role of health literacy, health promotion, and population screening in primary healthcare.
Critically analyse health care systems, identifying strengths, weaknesses, and opportunities for improvement in health care delivery.
workload_hours: 17 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials, interprofessional learning (IPL) and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Advanced palliative and end of life care in nursing contexts
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces you to advanced, evidence-based, clinically relevant palliative care practices to support patients; families and carers to facilitate quality and dignity at the end of life. This unit prepares you to work collaboratively with interprofessional teams across specialist and other care settings. You will develop a deeper understanding of local, national and international palliative and end of life care contexts; models of care; end of life communication; cultural and religious considerations; loss, grief and bereavement; medico-legal, and ethical issues; and care of professional carers.
learning_outcomes: Plan management for deteriorating patients and/or when patients are not responding well to interventional care in consideration of family and proxy decision makers
Demonstrate empathetic communication skills in end of life care contexts
Identify when patients are approaching the end of life and select appropriate models of care
Examine common issues associated with delivery of holistic palliative and end of life care in a variety of health care contexts
Identify strategies for building your own capability to manage and support end of life care in your area of practice
Discuss and facilitate advance care planning in practice

assessment_tasks.task_name: Part 1- Poster presentation & Part 2- Oral assessment

workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self directed study, including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Healthcare across the lifespan
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces you to nursing across the lifespan in a variety of healthcare settings. Founded in person and family centred care and evidence-based practice principles, the milestones and transitional periods across people's lives are explored. Socio-political and psychosocial factors that influence well-being and access to, and provision of healthcare are considered. Nursing roles and different models of care in terms of the changing needs of people across the lifespan, including those living with disability, chronic conditions, dementia and people requiring end of life care are examined.
learning_outcomes: Examine the key principles and approaches to persons and family centred care.
Identify key developmental milestones and life stages for the delivery of person and family centred nursing care.
Analyse approaches to effectively communicate with patients, their families and the healthcare team.
Critique the role of the nurse in caring for people across the lifespan, in different healthcare contexts.
Explore the socio-political and psychosocial factors that impact on people across the lifespan living with illness, chronic conditions, disability, cognitive decline, and dementia.
workload_hours: 3 hours of teacher directed study per week comprised of 1 x 3-hour tutorial (total 24 hrs) 9 hours per week of self-directed /online study (120hrs)

title: Recovery oriented mental health nursing practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: Recovery in mental health is a unique experience that is defined by the person. Recovery oriented mental health nursing practice aims to support people in their personal recovery from mental health conditions and uphold their rights as service users. In this unit you will examine approaches and frameworks used in mental health nursing practice to support people in their recovery, and reflect on the role that mental health nurses can have in supporting people, families and communities’ growth and wellbeing. You will explore the significance of the consumer movement and the markedly different notions of recovery. Human rights and the interplay with stigma and discrimination will be explored in the context of the impact on service users.
learning_outcomes: Propose and justify ways in which the mental health nurse can avoid and address injustices in practice to support a person’s rights and promote recovery.
Discuss the impact of stigma, discrimination and/or human rights violations on recovery
Analyse recovery as an approach to working with mental health service users
Examine recovery-oriented approaches and/or frameworks to mental health nursing practice
Compare and contrast the recovery model with common perspectives on understanding and treating mental health conditions
workload_hours: 12 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Fostering therapeutic interactions in mental health nursing practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this unit you will focus on mental health nurses most foundational forms of communication. The unit will focus on your capacity to be fully present, actively and appreciatively listen, reflexively understand, and sensitively explore your interactions and conversations with service users and their carers and families. You will learn to enhance counselling microskills, expand therapeutic communication and tolerate uncertainty in everyday clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Examine the therapeutic use of self when working with mental health service users
Demonstrate and justify counselling microskills to engage and support mental health service users
Analyse the fundamental principles of helping relationships in mental health nursing practice
Argue the need for mental health nurses to adopt a not-knowing perspective, suspending their professional and personal beliefs to understand the point of view of mental health service users
Critique your own clinical work through reflective practice.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Essay and multimedia communication (10 minute video + 1000 word written reflection)

workload_hours: 12 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Holistic mental health care
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: People experiencing mental health conditions experience poorer physical health and poorer health outcomes, and less access to services than people without mental health conditions. Mental health nurses can play a key role in being able to promote a holistic approach to health and wellbeing to support positive outcomes for people living with mental and physical health problems. You will examine the social determinants of health and wellbeing and how these factors shape inequalities in health, particularly for priority populations. You will develop strategies to address, support and promote mental and physical health when working with consumers, families, carers and supporters. This unit will support you in being able to work holistically to improve the health and wellbeing of people living with mental health conditions.
learning_outcomes: Critique national and state-based targets, policies and/or frameworks aimed at improving outcomes for people who are experiencing or have experienced mental health conditions
Evaluate how structures and systems within Australian society affect health and wellbeing for people living with mental health conditions
Plan evidence-based, holistic, person-centred approaches to support and promote mental and physical health of people living with mental health conditions
Analyse the impacts of mental health conditions on overall health and wellbeing
Distinguish priority populations within Australia and analyse the relationship between priority populations and poorer mental health
Analyse why people living with mental health conditions experience poorer health outcomes than the general population
Advocate for equitable, multi-level, person-centred and integrated approaches to health care for people who are living with mental health conditions.
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements

title: Communication and collaboration for clinical partnerships
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit builds upon the unit ‘fostering therapeutic interactions in mental health nursing’ and focuses on advanced communication and approaches for collaborative practice with stakeholders. Stakeholders include service users, carers and families, and interdisciplinary teams across settings. You will develop skills to collaboratively plan and evaluate care, with consideration to psychosocial interventions to support service users in their recovery. You will further focus on approaches to reduce the use of coercive practices and keeping service users safe from additional harm in genuinely therapeutic environments in their homes, local community settings, or in specialised mental health settings. This unit will also support you in exploring the importance of leadership in working in clinical partnerships.
learning_outcomes: Analyse approaches for de-escalation to reduce aggression and the use of coercive practices
Reflect on the key attributes required of a mental health nurse to facilitate collaboration and partnerships when working with service users
Justify the need for collaborative approaches to safety planning that balance duty of care with dignity of risk
Collaboratively plan and evaluate person-centred and recovery-focused care with stakeholders
Examine identity, professionalism and leadership in mental health nursing practice for genuine collaboration with stakeholders.
Determine appropriate psychosocial interventions for service users to support recovery
Analyse factors that may affect the outcomes of psychosocial interventions for service users

assessment_tasks.task_name: Care plan and presentation (1,800 words + 10 min presentation)

workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements

title: Cancer nursing 1
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: Cancer nursing requires specialised skills and knowledge to provide care to the complex needs of patients with cancer. This unit introduces the advanced knowledge and skills required of specialist cancer nurses, enabling you to implement contemporary and advanced nursing practice to provide optimal and holistic, person-centred care. This unit includes topics such as the epidemiology of cancer across the lifespan, diagnosis of cancer and goals of care, evidence-based treatment of cancer including new and emerging treatment, effective nursing management of complications of cancer, and treatment including oncology emergencies.
learning_outcomes: Perform clinically at a minimum required standard, in accordance with the National Cancer Nursing Education Project (EdCaN) ANMC Competency Standards for Registered Nurses – cancer control.
Apply health education and health promotion strategies for people with cancer using a person, family and/or community centred approaches.
Communicate knowledge skills associated with the care of people with cancer to others in a professional and empathetic manner.
Critically evaluate clinical information of patient deterioration and implement effective management strategies needed for optimal patient outcomes.
Apply the principles of systematic patient assessment using applied knowledge of human anatomy and physiology.
Plan, prioritise, implement and evaluate person centred care and specialist nursing management for a person with cancer.
Critically analyse clinical information to differentiate the underlying pathophysiological processes, aetiology and clinical manifestations related to cancer.
Apply the National Safety and Quality and Health Service Standards (NSQHS) principles to develop strategies aimed at improving the safety and quality of cancer care.
workload_hours: 12 credit point unit = 288 total hours per semester 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed study, including tutorial and online activities

title: Contemporary nursing in context 3
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit examines foundations of knowledge for nursing and education for clinical practice. Knowledge generation through research, and the application and dissemination of that knowledge, are central themes of this unit. The development of a research culture as the cornerstone of professional nursing is emphasized. Research processes from various traditions are examined and their specific relevance to nursing in diverse practice settings is explored. The significance of evidence-based nursing in the context of the contemporary health care environment is highlighted. As a key feature of this unit, knowledge transfer and translation is examined in primary, acute and rehabilitative settings. Strategies for peer teaching and health promotion through teaching are developed through exploration of theoretical concepts and practical application in the classroom setting.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the ethical principles underpinning the research process
Evaluate the effectiveness of a teaching session through reflection on practice
Recommend strategies for the dissemination of knowledge to facilitate improved health outcomes
Critically analyse the philosophical underpinnings, methodologies and principles of research relevant to nursing practice
Apply evidence-based educational practices to plan, design and deliver a teaching session using EBP in health care
Identify strategies for the translation of research evidence and its application to nursing practice.
Explain the concept of evidence-based practice (EBP) and its application to nursing practice
Analyse the concept of knowledge generation in professional nursing through the critique of research
Critique theories of teaching and learning

assessment_tasks.task_name: Demonstration & personal reflection (teaching & evaluation of the prepared lesson plan) 3,500 words

workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Cancer nursing 2
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit builds upon the foundations established in unit NUR5016 and extends your knowledge of advanced cancer nursing care using an evidence-based approach. This unit will prepare you to provide advanced care to cancer patients, symptom management and end of life care. The role of the specialist cancer nurse in the multidisciplinary team is examined including clinical leadership. You will learn about effective communication and therapeutic relationships with patient groups and families. This unit will cover topics such as cancer nursing for diverse communities and priority populations and transitions in care for people living with cancer.
learning_outcomes: Perform clinically at a minimum required standard, in accordance with the National Cancer Nursing Education Project (EdCaN) ANMC Competency Standards for Registered Nurses – cancer control
Analyse legal and ethical issues in palliative and end of life care for people living with cancer
Apply complex care planning and ongoing requirements for people with cancer
Communicate knowledge and skills associated with the care of people with cancer to others in a professional and empathetic manner
Plan effective transitions in care across different care programs and settings for people with cancer
Analyse the determinants of health impacting people affected by cancer including priority populations and diverse communities
Critically appraise multidisciplinary team communication and team leadership in cancer care
Evaluate symptom management in palliative and end of life care for patients and families
workload_hours: 12 credit point unit = 288 total hours per semester 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed study, including workshops and online activities

title: Neuroscience nursing
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: Care of the patient with a neuroscience condition requires specialised nursing skills and knowledge to address the complex needs of the patient. In this unit you will develop specialised knowledge and skills that will enable you to assess, plan, prioritise, implement and evaluate appropriate nursing care of the acute neuroscience patient. You will also implement health promotion and educational principles, while considering evidence-based practices for those with neuroscience conditions. This unit will enable you to develop an understanding of evidence-based treatment including new and emerging treatment and effective nursing management of complications.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the evidence-based practice when caring for a person with a neuroscience condition and their significant others.
Implement health promotion and educational principles in the care of a person with a neuroscience condition to ensure optimal health outcomes.
Evaluate how your advanced knowledge, skills and attitudes contribute to the profession of neuroscience nursing practice.
Plan, prioritize, implement, and evaluate specialist nursing assessment and management for individuals with neurological conditions.
Analyse clinical information to differentiate underlying pathophysiological processes, aetiology, and clinical manifestations related to neurological conditions.
Perform clinically at a minimum required standard in accordance with Australasian Neuroscience Nursing Association (ANNA) Professional standards for neuroscience nurses (ANNA).
Differentiate the purpose of multidisciplinary team collaborations in the management of an individual with neurological conditions considering the person, family, and/or community-centred approach.
Distinguish and justify the legal and ethical considerations of the patient with a neuroscience condition.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Clinical competency assessment and performance Appraisal (Pass/Fail)

workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed study, including tutorial and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Medical surgical nursing 1
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: Medical surgical nursing requires specialised skills and understanding of pathophysiology, assessment and management of patient care. In this unit you will be provided with an introduction to advanced medical surgical nursing principles and practice. You will develop skills to care for medical surgical patients using a patient centred approach. This unit will explore the essential elements involved in delivering and managing best evidence-based care for medical-surgical patients throughout their continuum from initial presentation to recovery. Through your study and development of communication skills you will support patients to participate in their care. You will enhance your skills in interprofessional communication, actively engage patients in their care and develop communication skills and leadership practices that improve patient outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate evidence-based pharmacological interventions to achieve safe outcomes for patients across a range of complex disease states.

Interpret patient assessment findings to inform advanced clinical decision making in the formulation and prioritisation of person-centre, evidence-based management of the medical surgical patient with complex healthcare needs.
Adopt effective communication skills and clinical leadership practices for holistic nursing care.
Develop strategies integrating the Australian National Safety and Quality and Health Service (NSQHS) Standards aimed at improving the safety and quality of care in the medical surgical environment.
Evaluate clinical information to differentiate the underlying pathophysiological processes, aetiology and clinical manifestations related to chronic and complex disease presentations.
Analyse and apply the principles of systematic patient assessment using applied knowledge of human anatomy and physiology.
Evaluate the effectiveness of care and management delivered to the medical surgical patient with complex healthcare needs.
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Medical surgical nursing 2
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: Medical surgical nursing requires specialised skills and understanding of clinical leadership, management, and patient care. You will develop skills to care for medical surgical patients using a patient-centred approach incorporating effective health promotion and health education strategies. Your study will include key factors associated with the management of medical surgical patients, stabilisation, and management of the seriously ill or deteriorating patients. You will examine the role of nurses in different contexts of medical surgical nursing including ethical considerations when working with patients and the interdisciplinary team.
learning_outcomes: Plan, deliver and evaluate advanced medical surgical nursing practice to manage patients with complex disease states.
Implement effective quality transitions in care for complex medical surgical patients between various levels of care and different health, aged care and social services.
Implement and evaluate end of life care to patients and families from diverse communities.
Evaluate complex care planning of medical surgical patients from different populations.
Evaluate the effectiveness of health promotion, health literacy and health education strategies for a range of medical surgical conditions
Evaluate clinical information to assess and manage patient deterioration for optimal patient outcomes.
Facilitate effective communication and advanced nursing leadership and management for medical surgical patients of different populations as per registered nurse standards.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Concept map and presentation (1,500 words and 5-minute presentation)

workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Contemporary nursing practice 1
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: The unit will provide you with the foundational knowledge and skills for nursing practice with an emphasis on physical health assessment. You will study key concepts, including pharmacology, asepsis, hygiene and a patient-centred approach to nursing care. Clinical practice experience is an integral component of this unit and concentrates on the attainment of skills, knowledge and competency in fundamental patient care.
learning_outcomes: Perform fundamental nursing skills to maintain and ensure patient safety using an evidence-based approach.
Reflect on, and evaluate, self performance related to knowledge, skills and delivery of nursing care.
Determine appropriate nursing care for a dying patient.
Integrate theory, clinical problem solving, communication and decision-making skills to systematically assess patients.
Evaluate patient assessment data to inform nursing care interventions.

Demonstrate practice at a beginning level in accordance with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) Registered nurse standards for practice, Code of conduct for nurses and the International Council of Nurses (ICN) Code of ethics for nurses.
Apply the principles of pharmacology to therapeutic drug administration and monitoring to ensure medication safety.
Plan, implement and evaluate of nursing care using a patient-centred approach.
Apply anatomical and physiological knowledge to patient assessment and care planning.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Case study analysis and reflection (2,000 words)
Case study analysis and reflection (2000 words)

workload_hours: 12 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials, clinical learning environments and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Nursing informatics
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: Relationships between computers, information technologies and the provision of health care. Contemporary issues in health informatics. Skills in the use of information technologies in health care settings enabling participants to act as a conduits, facilitating and enhancing communication between and among clinicians, technicians, information systems personnel, health care executives and systems vendors. Issues of privacy, ethics, confidentiality and network security.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the role of network security in maintaining information system integrity;
Discuss the role of data standards and case mix in health informatics;
Demonstrate an ability to competently utilise communication applications such as email, newsgroups, intranet and Internet audio/video technology and evaluate their benefits to health care;
Analyse and evaluate a number of information sources such as CD-ROM databases and websites related to healthcare knowledge in general and specifically to health Informatics;
Evaluate current trends in communication and network technology and their impact on Health Information Systems;
Demonstrate an understanding of current trends in health care and how they influence the development, implementation and utilisation of information systems;
Analyse a number of Clinical Information Systems and determine their role in improving health care.
Analyse a number of networking structures and topographies;

Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of how specific software application (e.g. word processing, spreadsheet, database, presentation and statistics) may be applied to healthcare practice, education, administration and research;
Understand issues related to informatics ethics, privacy and confidentiality;
Outline the role of various computer architectures in the provision of Information Systems;
Analyse a number of information technology implementation strategies and outline their impact on health Informatics;
Describe the role of database, communication and network technology in the development, implementation and utilisation of information systems;
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Education in health care practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit will offer you an evidence base for contemporary teaching and learning practice of health care practitioners, within a context of continuous change. You will explore a range of theoretical underpinnings that impact upon the educational process in health care practice with emphasis placed on educational learning theories. You will apply theoretical learning to teaching practice through design, plan and delivery of a teaching practicum and reflecting on their role as a teacher within your own clinical practice. This unit will examine flexible and innovative teaching strategies for both classroom and clinical teaching and supervision experiences in a variety of contexts, including inter-professional education. After completion of this unit, you will be equipped with the knowledge and mastery of skills to respond to health care practitioners learning needs, in order to enhance engagement and educational experiences.
learning_outcomes: Contrast and critique contemporary teaching and learning methods for a range of clinical and academic education contexts.
Develop your own teaching philosophy to justify your approaches in teaching practice.
Investigate and analyse a range of educational learning theories and their potential application to health professions’ education.
Evaluate your own teaching approaches in a teaching practicum.
Describe and critique common workplace, clinical supervision and teaching models.
Discuss contemporary active learning trends in health profession education.
Apply critical reflective skills through linking past and present learnings to future education in health care practice.
Evaluate current and future educational roles and contexts that encompass education in health care practice.
Apply evidence-based educational practices to plan, design and implement an education session for health care practitioners.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Lesson plan and oral presentation (Plan - 1,500 words; Oral presentation - 30 minutes)

workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Therapeutic medication management (Prescribing)
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit will enable you to apply the principles of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in the therapeutic management of medication in advanced practice settings. By demonstrating an understanding of prescribed medications on major body systems, you will be able to critically analyse medication regimes for discipline specific clinical conditions, utilising state and federal frameworks for clinical decision making. Examining your role in therapeutic medication management, you will gain a critical understanding of the legal, ethical and professional accountabilities for which you are responsible within your scope of practice and area of specialisation. This will include the requirements for you to evaluate the effect of the social determinants of health on therapeutic medication management outcomes. You will also demonstrate the knowledge of health education for clients regarding self-management of medications and learn the skills to safely and effectively prescribe medications within the Australian healthcare system, your scope of practice, and area of specialisation.
learning_outcomes: Explain the mechanism of action, clinical indication and therapeutic effect for commonly prescribed medications.
Apply the principles of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics to therapeutic medication management across a variety of clinical settings.
Determine your legal, ethical, and professional responsibilities in medication prescribing according to state, territory and federal legislation, within your scope of practice.
Propose educational strategies and non-pharmacological interventions that support medication adherence and improved health outcomes.
Critically appraise Quality Use of Medicines principles for evidence‑based medication management practices.
Optimise medication regimes for discipline specific conditions to improve a person's health and wellbeing.
Distinguish the implications of social, cultural, environmental, and political factors influencing the use of medications on health outcomes.
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials, interprofessional learning and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Education program development
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: Health professions’ educators need to acquire knowledge and skills to assess, design and develop contemporary, learner-centred education programs. This unit introduces learners to health education research and scholarship that supports evidence-based teaching and learning practices. This flexible unit will offer you the opportunity to work through the process of education program development and apply evidence-based teaching and learning strategies relevant to an education context. It will also prepare you with the knowledge and skills to comprehensively assess and evaluate the outcomes of the education program..
learning_outcomes: Analyse contemporary literature related to assessment and evaluation principles and apply these to the development of an education program in healthcare practice/education.
Examine and apply contemporary factors that influence education program development in healthcare practice/education.
Examine models of curriculum designs relevant to education and healthcare practice.
Analyse how innovative teaching methods can impact healthcare educational program development.
Conduct an education needs assessment (ENA) in your workplace, and analyse the results to identify goals and objectives related to learning needs of healthcare learners.
Appraise education research and its application in healthcare environments.
Apply evidence-based educational practices to plan, design and develop an education program.
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Disaster management in healthcare
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces you to the core elements of Emergency Management, inclusive of disaster classifications, theoretical frameworks and risk reduction concepts. In this unit, you will examine the key determinants of quality leadership, international competencies in disaster nursing, and safe and ethical concepts to enhance resilience amongst healthcare professionals.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the Global Disaster Risk Reduction concepts impact on local, national and international healthcare settings.
Assess the value and quality of leadership skills needed when striving for disaster resilience in healthcare settings.
Differentiate the roles of command, control and collaboration across healthcare settings when responding to disaster events.
Describe and evaluate the resources available to enhance resilience of the healthcare workforce in times of disasters.
Identify the concepts of the safe hospital index and apply these to any healthcare setting in a disaster event.
Identify the classifications and severity of disaster incidents impacting healthcare settings.
Identify the special needs of vulnerable populations in disaster situations.
Examine universal disaster theoretical frameworks used to mitigate impacts on healthcare settings.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Oral presentation (15 mins up to 20 slides)

workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Advanced symptom management in palliative and end of life care
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces you to advanced symptom management in palliative and end of life care. Working with patients in the palliative and end of life phase of illness requires specific knowledge and skills to manage complex symptoms and support quality patient outcomes. This unit will prepare you to understand complex symptoms from different types of health conditions, and provide palliative and end of life care in complex care situations. You will develop the skills to lead interdisciplinary teams and support the patient and their carers to achieve the desired outcomes. These functions require advanced knowledge and skills in symptom management, advanced therapeutics (pharmacological and non-pharmacological) and leadership.
learning_outcomes: Analyse effective therapeutic medication management in palliative and end of life care
Examine complex issues associated with delivery of holistic palliative and end of life care in a variety of health care contexts
Identify complex palliative and end of life care needs of priority populations
Apply palliative care leadership strategies in your area of practice
Identify management challenges in malignant and end stage chronic illness
Develop support strategies for building capability in health professionals and inter-professional teams to manage and support end of life care in your area of practice
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self directed study, including lectures, tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Mental health nursing concepts and practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit will equip you with the core knowledge and skills required of a mental health nurse to work collaboratively with service users to support and promote their journeys towards recovery. You will examine mental health conditions that are experienced across the lifespan, develop skills in assessment, and explore pharmacological and psychosocial approaches to support symptom management and recovery. Additionally, you will explore mental health nursing practice with consideration of law and ethics to support care delivery, safe practice and optimal health outcomes for service users, their families, carers and supporters.
learning_outcomes: Examine the role of the mental health nurse in the delivery of person-centred, recovery-oriented and/or trauma-informed care.
Examine the role of the mental health nurse in the use of non-pharmacological and pharmacological approaches to treat mental health conditions and/or symptoms
Apply knowledge of holistic assessments when supporting service users
Analyse mental health nursing approaches with consideration of evidence-based practice that supports service users’ mental health and their recovery
Plan, implement and evaluate person-centred nursing interventions to support recovery
Integrate knowledge of psychotropic medications used in mental health practice to support service users’ mental health and their recovery
Apply relevant legislation to decision-making in mental health nursing practice with consideration of ethics
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Advanced cardiac nursing care
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this unit you will build on and extend upon your knowledge and skills that have been gained from previous studies. The aim of this unit is to develop advanced knowledge and practice skills when caring for patients with a variety of cardiovascular conditions. You will learn about evidence-based management of acute and chronic cardiovascular conditions. This will include nursing care in relation to advanced monitoring and therapeutics, surgical and other procedural interventions, structural heart disease, complex arrhythmias, and culturally diverse and priority populations. You will practice and exemplify leadership and teamwork skills as a cardiac nurse.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced knowledge of pathophysiology to the assessment and management of patients with cardiovascular conditions.
Synthesise evidence-based practice to optimise cardiovascular health outcomes.
Assess and exemplify teamwork and leadership skills as a cardiac nurse.
Practice professionally at a minimum standard in accordance with the Practice Standards for Australian Cardiovascular Nursing.
Apply and evaluate safe and effective cardiovascular care to priority populations including culturally diverse populations.
Interpret a range of assessment data to inform a plan of nursing care.
Prioritise, implement, and evaluate person centred care and specialist nursing management for a person with cardiovascular conditions including comorbidities.
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed study, including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Foundations of cardiac nursing
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: Cardiac nursing requires specialised knowledge and advanced clinical skills essential to work in a variety of specialist cardiac settings. In this unit you will develop a comprehensive knowledge of the pathophysiology, epidemiology, assessment and management of patients with cardiovascular disease, associated respiratory conditions and comorbidities. This unit will enable you to develop specialist cardiac nursing knowledge and clinical skills to provide comprehensive person-centred, evidence-based care. You will also further develop your teamwork and leadership skills in the practice of cardiac nursing.
learning_outcomes: Identify and interpret assessment data to prioritise therapeutic interventions for patients experiencing cardiovascular disease
Appraise how teamwork and leadership skills can support the role of the cardiac nurse.
Analyse cardiovascular risk factors for diverse populations.
Formulate and implement complex care provided to a patient with cardiovascular disease and evaluate outcomes.
Apply knowledge of pathophysiology to the nursing management of patients with cardiovascular disease
Apply evidence-based practice in the provision of cardiac nursing care.
Practice professionally at a minimum standard in accordance with the Practice Standards for Australian Cardiovascular Nursing
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self directed study, including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Health professional leadership during disasters
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces you to disaster health management and the role of leadership within the multidisciplinary healthcare workforce during a disaster incident. In this unit you will examine effective health professional leadership decision–making, and review government policies and guidelines including risk assessment and business continuity planning. You will also explore disaster preparedness in multiple healthcare settings, and gain an understanding of the importance of educating future health professionals in disaster preparedness.
learning_outcomes: Promote educating future health professionals in disaster preparedness
Understand and apply government policies and guidelines that healthcare settings are required to use in their management for disaster events
Prioritise the requirements for Business Continuity planning in the context of disaster risk reduction
Identify the concepts of the safe hospital index and apply these to any healthcare setting in a disaster event
Analyse how health professional leaders communicate during the challenges of crisis management and evaluate the effectiveness of the communication
Discuss disaster preparedness of healthcare settings related to natural disasters climate change impacts
Select effective health professional leadership decision-making and risk-averse skills under the uncertainty of a low probability but high consequence disaster event.
workload_hours: 12 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Interventional cardiology nursing
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this unit you will be introduced to the highly specialised area of interventional cardiology nursing, in order to care for a diverse cohort of patients, who range from low acuity to critically ill, and requiring life-saving interventions. As a nurse who may work in this area, you require specific cardiac knowledge to provide safe and holistic care to patients undergoing interventional cardiology procedures. In this unit, as part of the multidisciplinary team, you will also develop the knowledge that will enable you to provide support and education for patients in the cardiac catheterisation laboratory and their significant others. You will also develop the skills required to manage the patient at all stages of their catheterisation laboratory journey; understanding and managing interventional equipment, and provide advanced nursing practice in this unique nursing setting.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the pathophysiology of cardiac conditions associated with interventional cardiology.
Review and critique the evidence-based practice underpinning selected interventional cardiology procedures or conditions.
Propose ways in which interventional cardiology nurses can contribute to teamwork and leadership within the context of the catheterisation laboratory environment.
Assess, plan and analyse the case of culturally diverse patients undergoing interventional cardiology procedures.
Apply advanced nursing practice knowledge to the role and work of interventional cardiology nursing.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Educational plan (1,500 words) and presentation (15 mins)

title: Leading improvement and innovation in the quality and safety of health care
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit enables you to understand and apply contemporary approaches, tools and techniques to improving the quality and safety of health care and services. The historical and contemporary context, purpose of, and approaches to improvement and innovation in health care are explored. Working within the framework of the National Safety and Quality Health Service Standards (Version 2), you will utilise contemporary technologies and approaches used to identify clinical performance gaps, and develop person-centred outcomes for improvement and innovation.
learning_outcomes: Critique the historical and contemporary context for improving the quality and safety of health care in Australia and internationally.
Identify evidence relating to the presence, risks and approaches to addressing specific care quality and safety issues in health professional practice.
Apply contemporary approaches and techniques in developing plans and interventions for improving the quality and safety of health care.
Describe the role of clinical governance in the prevention and minimisation of clinical risks and adverse outcomes in health professional practice.
Critique approaches and techniques for improving specific care quality and safety issues in contemporary health professional practice.
workload_hours: 12 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Clinical leadership in healthcare
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: The aim of this unit is to research and apply modern leadership theories to healthcare practice. The content is delivered in three modules. The first module examines concepts of the development of clinical leadership performance and skills. The second explores contemporary leadership theories and considers their relevance to healthcare leadership in a range of clinical contexts. The third examines developmental strategies in healthcare that require operationalisation of clinical leadership.
learning_outcomes: Identify contemporary clinical leadership attributes and their application in healthcare settings.
Analyse leadership strategies that enable the individual to determine their own individual style in healthcare settings.
Evaluate interventions in healthcare settings that contribute to the development of leadership capabilities.
Demonstrate ability to apply leadership strategies in healthcare settings.
Evaluate clinical development outcomes produced through leadership intervention.
Critically analyse leadership theories relevant to professional nursing or midwifery practice and their application in healthcare settings.
workload_hours: 12 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Management and leadership in healthcare practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit examines the concepts of management and leadership as applied to the conduct of health professional practice. The content is delivered in four modules. The first module examines key professional and organisational structures that govern the scope and practice of health professionals’ work in particular healthcare contexts. The uses and roles of policy (development, utilisation and compliance) in assisting governance will be studied. In the second module, contemporary methods for the organisation of work in healthcare environments will be examined including human resources management. These also will be considered in relation to industry and technology reforms; political, business and social agendas; and developmental strategies. The third module examines principles and models for strategic planning and operational interventions for the management and development of health services and work. The fourth module examines the role of interdisciplinary engagement and activities in relation to health professional leadership and management strategies.
learning_outcomes: Critique contemporary methods of organising health professional work in a range of practice contexts
Critique commonly used strategies for strategic planning and operational implementation in particular healthcare workplace contexts
Evaluate the implementation of a specific management and leadership strategy in the conduct of health professional work

Distinguish between leadership and management principles to influence health services and professional organisations to enhance the voice of health professionals in improving the quality of service delivery and health policy development.
Critically debate professional and workplace governance structures that have been proven to be successful in particular healthcare workplace contexts.
Recommend techniques related to enhancing interdisciplinary engagement that can be used in health professional leadership and management situations
Apply leadership and management principles to a health professional practice setting to ensure delivery of safe, quality care
Compare and contrast leadership and management responsibilities and outcomes associated with the organisation of health professional practice.

Differentiate drivers for change (e.g. industry and technology reforms; political, business and social agendas) and proactively lead health professional responses to changing and dynamic environments.
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including tutorials and online activities. Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Advanced clinical decision making
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit builds on NUR5411 in the consultation sequence exploring the advanced management of common conditions. It further extends your knowledge and skills relating to the clinical reasoning process to enable you to plan and implement evidence-informed interventions. You will develop the skills required to analyse the clinical, cultural and professional factors that influence nurse practitioner clinical decision making. This includes promoting a holistic model of care and recognition of and respect for cultural identity and lifestyle choices. Additionally, in this unit you will examine contemporary professional issues that impact upon nurse practitioner practice and inform the scope of the nurse practitioner role in specific practice areas.
learning_outcomes: Illustrate the role of health informatics and how it impacts upon nurse practitioner practice.
Evaluate the role of the nurse practitioner in primary care settings.
Articulate the professional, legal and ethical responsibilities associated with the nurse practitioner role.
Analyse the nurse practitioner’s role in provision of culturally safe care.
Validate evidence-based therapeutic interventions in Nurse Practitioner practice.
Implement advanced practice clinical decisions cognisant of biopsychosocial and cultural factors that impact health and wellbeing.
Critique contemporary professional issues that support and/or challenge the nurse practitioner scope of practice.
prerequisites: NUR5411: Advanced clinical assessment and diagnostic reasoning
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including lectures, tutorials, online activities and supernumerary integrated professional practice (SIPP). Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Advanced clinical assessment and diagnostic reasoning
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit enables you to focus on the acquisition and synthesis of advanced nursing knowledge and skills related to the initial aspect of the consultation sequence - specifically, advanced history taking, advanced health assessment, the formulation of a working diagnosis and differentials, and the ordering and interpretation of diagnostic tests. Additionally, you will analyse the impact of social determinants of health on history taking and health assessment and how these factors influence your diagnostic reasoning.
learning_outcomes: Formulate clinical impressions by​ systematically synthesising patient history, health assessment and diagnostic tests.
Interpret and evaluate clinical assessment findings to inform relevant investigative options.
Analyse the context of social determinants of health on history taking, health assessment and how these impact upon diagnostic reasoning.
Create and conduct an educational session in the advanced practice role.
Articulate an advanced holistic health assessment of the patient in a succinct and structured manner.
workload_hours: 24 hours per week of teacher facilitated and self-directed learning including lectures, tutorials, online activities and supernumerary integrated professional practice (SIPP). Please refer to Moodle for tutorial types and requirements.

title: Trauma nursing 1
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: Nurses working in different contexts of trauma care require specialist trauma knowledge and the skill-base to assess and manage trauma patients throughout their journeys.
