title: Advancing skills in paediatric physiotherapy: Cerebral palsy
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit will cover components of physiotherapy assessment and management options for children with cerebral palsy who present to physiotherapists. Aetiology and epidemiology of cerebral palsy, and the physiotherapy role in evaluation and management of children with this condition are described. An emphasis on establishing competence and confidence to work autonomously whilst identifying limits to own practice is stressed. Learning will be experienced in the online classroom environment with a single face to face day at the conclusion of the unit. A selection of case studies drawn from the acute, subacute and community settings will be used to explore learning outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate sensitive and appropriate communication at all times when working with children, their parents/carers
Identify and describe the principles of physiotherapy management in cerebral palsy
Describe the advantages and disadvantages of burst versus ongoing therapy prescription across childhood in cerebral palsy within a multidisciplinary framework
Demonstrate appropriate and professional communication with other health care professionals, both internal and external to their own health care setting.
Synthesise the complexities around transition from paediatric to adult services in adolescents with cerebral palsy using a multidisciplinary framework
Identify and select appropriate outcome measures for children with cerebral palsy across the age span using the ICF model
Summarise the complexity in equipment prescription in cerebral palsy across the life span
Describe relevant embryology in regards to the timing of cerebral insults that result in a diagnosis of cerebral palsy and an understanding of common risk factors leading to the diagnosis

assessment_tasks.task_name: Online exam (MCQ and short answers) (1 hour)
Contribution to 4 x discussion boards (One per module, as per unit guide)
Attendance requirement (Face to face day, available also via video footage)

workload_hours: Approximately 12 hours per week of interaction with online lectures and course material, completion of online assessment tasks and participation in online communications with other students and tutor (online delivery only, block mode), plus self-directed study time. An additional 8 hours of face to face day attendance or video footage viewing required.

title: Advancing skills in paediatric physiotherapy: Neonates and infants
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit will cover components of physiotherapy assessment and management options for neonates and infants with a range of conditions who present to physiotherapists. Aetiology and epidemiology of examples of conditions experienced by neonates and infants, and the physiotherapy role in evaluation of neonates and infants are described. An emphasis on establishing competence and confidence to work autonomously whilst identifying limits to own practice is stressed. Learning will be experienced in the online classroom environment with a single face to face day at the conclusion of the unit. A selection of case studies drawn from the special care nursery, subacute and community settings will be used to explore learning outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Critique the evidence relating to physiotherapy interventions for neonates and infants and apply this to justify clinical decision-making.
Apply the phases of foetal/neonatal neurological and respiratory development in clinical decision-making.
Appraise psychometric properties and clinical application of standardised outcome measures for the assessment of individual neonates and infants.
Apply knowledge of typical child development to the clinical physiotherapy management of neonates and infants.
Justify physiotherapy plans for neonates and infants based on comprehensive musculoskeletal and neurodevelopmental assessments, consistent with clinical best practice.
Evaluate the principles of developmental care and apply these to clinical practice with neonates.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Attendance requirement (face to face day, available also via video footage)
Contribution to 4 x discussion boards (one per module as per unit guide instructions)

workload_hours: Approximately 12 hours per week of interaction with online lectures and course material, completion of online assessment tasks and participation in online communications with other students and tutor (online delivery only, block mode), plus self-directed study time. An additional 8 hours of face to face day attendance or video footage viewing required.

title: Advancing skills in paediatric physiotherapy: Complex and chronic conditions
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit will cover components of physiotherapy assessment and management options for children of all ages with a range of complex and chronic conditions. Aetiology and epidemiology of chronic and complex conditions experienced by paediatric clients, and the physiotherapy role in evaluation are described. An emphasis on establishing competence and confidence to work autonomously whilst identifying limits to own practice is stressed. Learning will be experienced in the online classroom environment with a single face to face day at the conclusion of the unit. A selection of case studies drawn from acute, subacute and community settings will be used to explore learning outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Describe the aetiology and pathophysiology of progressive neuromuscular disorders, acquired brain injury, persistent pain and chronic fatigue in the paediatric population and integrate this knowledge into physiotherapy management of clients who have these conditions.
Justify the choice of appropriate standardised outcome measures.
Synthesise the evidence underpinning appropriate physiotherapy treatment selection.
Critically analyse the key elements of assessment and combine them into a relevant, feasible and comprehensive physiotherapy assessment.
Critically analyse the key elements of physiotherapy treatment and combine them into a relevant, feasible and comprehensive physiotherapy treatment plan.
Plan physiotherapy assessment and management within the context of the multi-disciplinary team and family-centred practice.
workload_hours: Approximately 12 hours per week of interaction with online lectures and course material, completion of online assessment tasks and participation in online communications with other students and tutor and self-directed study time (online delivery only, block mode). An additional 8 hours of face to face day attendance or video footage viewing required.

title: Advanced physiotherapy clinical skills and project
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This final unit will allow consolidation of advanced clinical practice. Skills in critical decision-making and clinical reasoning ability for the management of complex conditions will be emphasised. Problem solving and advanced clinical skills within the context of client or family-centred practice will be explored. Learning will be experienced in the online classroom environment with individually tailored clinical experiences.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the evidence underpinning relevant physiotherapy practice, including individual research studies, systematic reviews and clinical practice guidelines
Answer a clinical question exploring an issue in advanced physiotherapy practice.
Lead discussion of specific patient cases, with an advanced level of clinical reasoning.
Evaluate an intervention to address an issue in advanced physiotherapy practice.
Summarise findings from a project and present them, consistent with the standards of a professional conference.
Apply the principles of reflective learning and self-assessment to develop your own professional learning goals and formulate a plan to meet those goals.
Evaluate the effectiveness of episodes of paediatric physiotherapy care.
Evaluate the key performance characteristics of an advanced practice physiotherapist.
workload_hours: Approximately 12 hours per week of interaction with online lectures and course material, completion of assessment tasks and participation in online communications with other students and tutor, plus an equal amount of self-directed study time. An additional up to 5 days of individualised clinical experience will be scheduled.

title: Foundations of physiotherapy
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces the four themes of the physiotherapy course, facilitating integration of prior science and theoretical learning into the context of physiotherapy. The attributes of the physiotherapy profession, and its role in the broader health care system are introduced with an analysis of the diverse interpretations of health, the biopsychosocial model and determinants of health. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander concepts of health and wellbeing and the influence of culture, family and connection to country in health practice are explored. Anatomy, biomechanics and kinesiology theory are applied to normal and abnormal movement and exercise prescription and health promotion principles are studied. The multi-dimensional nature of pain and underpinning theory are introduced. A health enhancement program emphasises strategies for facilitating personal health and wellbeing and the research theme applies evidence based practice to clinical questions. Self-directed preparation activities precede weekly applied anatomy and exercise practical sessions and additional theoretical content is covered in interactive lectures, workshops and tutorials. You participate in work integrated learning visits to facilitate early exposure to the practice of physiotherapy in clinical settings.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of the anatomy, physiology and biomechanics of the limbs and spine to common conditions encountered in physiotherapy practice.
Design and implement evidence-based, safe exercise interventions for individuals with a range of health conditions and activity levels.
Analyse health-related data by executing quantitative analysis to investigate comparisons and associations between variables.
Appraise levels of research evidence, study design and sources of bias that inform person-centred physiotherapy care.
Evaluate service delivery models within Australian healthcare systems and explain the roles and responsibilities of members of the healthcare team.
Analyse the influence of culture and connection to country on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples’ concepts of health and wellbeing to inform culturally safe practice.
Analyse and compare health and health promotion frameworks across individual, cultural, and population contexts.
Adapt professional communication and collaborative practice to diverse contexts through reflexive evaluation and improvement of personal performance.
Justify evidence-informed strategies to improve personal and community determinants of health that promote sustainable health outcomes.
Practice ethical and professional conduct consistent with physiotherapy practice thresholds as a beginning-level practitioner.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Determinants of Health presentation (20 min group presentation)
Applied Anatomy Assessments (quizzes x 2, oral assessment 40 mins)
Exercise prescription and program design case study ( 15 mins and up to 1,000 words)

workload_hours: On-campus: 3-4 hours of lectures and seminars, 11-12 hours of tutorials including clinical skills, research and applied anatomy sessions, and 10 hours of self-directed activity expected each week Off-campus: You are also required to attend two work-integrated learning placement days over the duration of the semester.

title: Musculoskeletal physiotherapy
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit will focus on the knowledge and skills required for physiotherapy assessment and management of clients with musculoskeletal conditions. The theoretical features of pathology and pathophysiology are applied to musculoskeletal conditions involving the spine, upper limb and lower limb. The legal and ethical concepts of clinical practice are introduced, in addition to strategies to identify risk to self and others. Knowledge of the science of pain and person-centred strategies for management of pain are applied to clinical cases and contemporary theories of learning introduced. Preparation activities precede weekly practical, skills and simulation sessions. Clinical application is introduced in a case based learning format. Weekly practical sessions and simulation sessions ensure there are multiple opportunities for skills practice and feedback. Additional theoretical content is covered in interactive lectures, workshops and tutorials.
learning_outcomes: Appraise and apply effective communication strategies with clients and colleagues in a simulated clinical environment.
Employ reflection and self-evaluation to support the development of professional skills as a beginning-level practitioner.
Exhibit evidence based clinical reasoning in the management of clients with musculoskeletal conditions.
Apply legal and ethical concepts to healthcare practice.
Implement risk minimisation strategies ensuring safe physiotherapy practice for self and others.
Synthesise knowledge of pathophysiology, biomechanics and anatomy to perform evidence-informed musculoskeletal assessment and management.
Apply principles of pain science in the assessment and management of person-centred physiotherapy practice.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Case-based learning (CBL) performance (12 written learning issues of approximately 300 words each)
Professional Practice Portfolio (1500 words and three video submissions)
Objective Structured Clinical Examination (48 minutes including reading time)
Application of Knowledge - musculoskeletal physio theory (2x45 mins tests + 2 hr 10 mins exam)

workload_hours: 6-7 hours of lectures and seminars, 8-9 hours of tutorials including case-based learning, clinical skills and simulation sessions, and 10 hours of self-directed activity expected each week

title: Neurological physiotherapy
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: Within this unit, you will focus on the knowledge and skills required for physiotherapy assessment and management of clients with neurological conditions. There is an emphasis on person-centred and evidence-based approaches to neurological physiotherapy. Normal childhood development will be introduced to you, prior to analysis of developmental delay and the introduction of skills for working with the paediatric population. You will then be introduced to the theoretical features of pathology and pathophysiology which are applied to neurological conditions. In this unit you will have the opportunity to not only build strategies for effective communication with clients with neurological disease but also the broader health care team, ensuring that mechanisms for minimising risk to both clients and self are reinforced. Your research skills will be extended to demonstrate the use of reliable and valid assessment tools and the critical appraisal of research using a quality appraisal tool. Your clinical reasoning will be developed with a case-based learning format, and required engagement in weekly practical and simulation sessions. You are also required to participate in interprofessional simulation and work integrated learning visits, to prepare for the practice of physiotherapy in clinical settings.
learning_outcomes: Identify the principles of motor skill acquisition across the lifespan;
Analyse factors contributing to abnormal function in the person with neurological impairments;
Describe a range of pathophysiological disorders and mechanisms of recovery of neurological system and relate these to physiotherapy management;

Distinguish and compare the roles and responsibilities of the physiotherapist and other members of the health care team in the management of the client with stable or progressive neurological disease;

Apply knowledge of health sciences to determine and perform appropriate neurological physiotherapy management across the lifespan, including monitoring its effectiveness, discharge planning and utilising re-assessment findings to inform practice;
Implement a range of strategies that enable effective communication with clients with stable or progressive neurological disease and their caregivers;
Design and conduct an appropriate, timely assessment of the neurological system, including determination of client’s short and long-term goals and medico-legal documentation of findings;
Identify the policy and related funding issues surrounding care and treatment of the client with stable or progressive neurological disease;
Apply anatomical knowledge to the function of the neurological system;
Demonstrate appropriate, safe and effective manual handling and positioning of self and client at all times, utilising principles of risk minimisation;
Critically appraise clinical research using appropriate quality appraisal tools;
Explain evidence based physiotherapy interventions relevant to the management of the neurological client;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) (60 mins total)

workload_hours: 5-6 hours of lectures, 12-13 hours of tutorials including case-based learning, clinical skills and simulation sessions, and 10 hours of self-directed activity expected each week

title: Cardiorespiratory physiotherapy
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit will focus on the knowledge and skills required for physiotherapy assessment and management of clients with cardiorespiratory conditions. Person-centred and evidence based approaches to cardiorespiratory physiotherapy are emphasised. The theoretical features of pathology and pathophysiology are applied to a range of cardiorespiratory conditions. Strategies for working with the broader health team are prioritised, and mechanisms for minimising risk to both clients and self are reinforced. Online preparation activities precede weekly practical, skills and simulation sessions. Clinical reasoning is developed through the analysis of clinical cases, practical training and simulation sessions, to ensure there are multiple opportunities for skills practice and feedback. Additional theoretical content includes interactive lectures, workshops and tutorials. You participate in an interprofessional simulation and work integrated learning visits, to prepare for the practice of physiotherapy in clinical settings.
learning_outcomes: Describe the pathophysiology of injury and disease of the cardiorespiratory system and relate this to physiotherapy management;
Explain the anatomical structure and function of the thorax (including the cardiorespiratory system) and abdomen;
Apply knowledge of commonly encountered medications (including analgesics, anticoagulants, anti-infectives) to physiotherapy practice;

Determine and perform appropriate cardiorespiratory physiotherapy management across the lifespan, including monitoring its effectiveness, discharge planning and utilising re-assessment findings to inform practice;
Design and conduct a physiotherapy assessment of the cardiorespiratory system including determination of a client’s short and long-term goals and medico-legal documentation of findings;
Implement a range of strategies that enable effective communication with clients with cardiorespiratory disease and their caregivers;
Communicate appropriate information to other health professionals involved in providing client care to optimize interprofessional management;
Apply evidence based clinical reasoning to devise a client-centred problem list;
Calculate and interpret statistics to support clinical decision making in physiotherapy interventions.
Demonstrate appropriate manual handling and positioning of self and client at all times, utilising principles of risk minimisation;
Explain evidence-based physiotherapy interventions relevant to the management of the cardiorespiratory client;
Identify the issues surrounding care and treatment of the client with acute or chronic cardiorespiratory conditions;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Applied anatomy and physiology test (90 mins, plus 10 mins reading time)
Research Tests (30 minutes permitted for each test).
OSCE (60 mins: 20 mins reading time, 20 mins Ax station, 20 mins Rx station)

workload_hours: On campus: 4 hours of lectures, 1.5 hours of seminars, 1 hour of workshops and 11-12 hours of tutorials including case-based learning, clinical skills, applied anatomy, physiotherapy theory, simulation and 7 hours of self-directed activity expected each week. An additional workshop of 3.5 hours will be held on a single day during the term. Off campus: Students are also required to attend two work integrated learning placement days.

title: Clinical practice 1
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this clinical placement unit, you will be required to complete a 5-week full time clinical placement in either an acute, subacute/ rehabilitation setting. This unit will enable you to build upon your knowledge and experience to develop the competencies required for independent practice as a physiotherapist. Through supervised practice, you will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge and skills in assessment, treatment and client education, whilst working as part of a larger health care team. The professional, ethical and legal aspects of physiotherapy will be applied to practice, providing an opportunity to develop technical, clinical, personal and professional skills. Additional study includes an analysis of client transitions through health services and the use of audit to improve clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Identify, critically appraise and apply evidence-based practice to client care in physiotherapy;
Communicate appropriately and effectively across written and verbal mediums, with clients, staff, and other health care stakeholders;
Reflect critically on practice and propose knowledge and skill gaps and methods for ongoing learning;
Demonstrate professional behaviour in client care and rights that is culturally sensitive and in accordance with legal requirements;
Appraise clinical practice guidelines used in physiotherapy practice.
Tailor knowledge and skills to effectively assess client needs, including selection of relevant measures of health indicators and outcomes;
Analyse and plan appropriate patient interactions, including patient-centred goal development, and the selection of appropriate interventions;
Seek, reflect on and respond appropriately to feedback from others in the practice context and analyse strategies for successful management of stress and fatigue on physical and mental health;
Critically analyse risks and adverse events associated with client assessments and interventions;
Describe and analyse a client's transition to a new context, referral for further physiotherapy and linkage to relevant clinical and non-clinical support services

assessment_tasks.task_name: Clinical practice guideline appraisal (2,400 words equivalent)
Assessment of Physiotherapy Practice (5-week clinical placement)

workload_hours: Off-campus clinical placement: You will be allocated 32 contact hours per week for 5 weeks. Variations to placement hours may occur due to public holidays, host organisation factors, or student absences. Make-up placement time may be offered at the discretion of the Department and only when convenient for the organisation in which the placement is taking place. In addition to contact hours, you are expected to complete approximately 8 hours/week of self-directed study related to your clinical placement. Off-campus: During the 7 weeks where you are not on clinical placement, an average of 16 hours of online modules and private study is required weekly.

title: Integrated practice
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this unit, you will focus on integrating the knowledge and skills learnt from the prior foundations, musculoskeletal, neurological and cardiorespiratory units into practice in preparation for the complexity that is commonly encountered in clinical practice. Differences in the role of the physiotherapy in emergency, acute, subacute and community settings are explored. The development of your clinical reasoning will encompass the differences in the role of physiotherapy in emergency, acute, subacute and community. The role of physiotherapy in a variety of areas of physiotherapy practice is explored including oncology, women's and men’s health, amputees, chronic pain, falls, and vestibular conditions. Biopsychosocial perspectives are analysed within complex presentations, including a focus on developing your cultural capability. Systematic literature review tasks are completed in response to a clinical question, in preparation for the capstone independent research project in the Doctor of Physiotherapy. The unit is comprised of two components: an on-campus workshop and simulation block, and off campus learning modules focused on the role of physiotherapy in imaging and domestic violence. Preparation activities precede the on-campus practical skills and simulation sessions, to ensure there are multiple opportunities for skills practice and feedback. A dedicated pre-clinical week will prepare you for the clinical placements that follow. Off campus modules are completed between clinical placement blocks.
learning_outcomes: Recognise common presentations of family violence in healthcare and describe best practice for management if encountered by a physiotherapist;
Conduct a systematic review in accordance with recommended methods such as those outlined in the Cochrane handbook.
Define and explain pain to others as a complex, multidimensional experience;
Synthesise the pathophysiology of injury and disease from multiple systems and integrate knowledge into physiotherapy assessment and management;

Apply physiotherapy management in specialised areas of practice, including clients presenting with complaints relating to oncology, women’s health, amputees, chronic pain, vestibular, falls, dementia and complex musculoskeletal conditions;

Communicate appropriate information to other health professionals involved in providing client care to optimize interprofessional management, including medical and surgical, behavioural and psychological, or pharmacological approaches;
Compare the belief structures behind mainstream and complementary therapies, and their efficacy in therapy;
Utilise data from imaging or investigation results to inform clinical reasoning; and
Apply knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the endocrine, renal, reproductive and vestibular systems and their common pathologies to physiotherapy management and client care;
Describe how ethnicity and culture influence health, healthcare and illness;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Systematic review tasks (Written task-2,500 words & oral presentation-10-15 mins - group)
OSCE - 2 x 20 minute stations plus 20 minute reading time
Learning skills portfolio (Approx. 1.5 - 2 hours per week of post-class tasks)

workload_hours: On-campus block (6 weeks) - 3-4 hours of seminars and 3-4 hours of lectures, 7-10 hours of tutorials including clinical skills, tutorials and simulation sessions and 10 hours of self-directed activity expected each week Off-campus block (6 weeks) - An average of 20 hours per week is required to complete the compulsory online modules and independent study

title: Disability and chronic disease
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this clinical placement unit you will be required to complete both a campus based block of study and a disability or chronic disease focused clinical placement. This unit will enable you to build upon your knowledge and experience to further develop the competencies required for working within the community to promote independence and physical ability across the lifespan. The two-week campus based intensive will expose you to expert practice in a range of masterclasses, focused on ethical and culturally sensitive client driven, integrated practice. Paediatric physiotherapy knowledge and skills will be further developed. Processes for utilising support from Aboriginal Health Workers and other Indigenous health professionals will be introduced. Through the supervised clinical practice placement, you will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge and skills in assessment, treatment and client education, whilst working as part of a larger health care team. The professional, ethical and legal aspects of physiotherapy will be applied to practice, providing an opportunity to develop technical, clinical, personal and professional skills.
learning_outcomes: Recognise the health policy and funding models aligned to the physiotherapy treatment of disability and chronic disease;
Critically analyse risks and adverse events associated with client assessments and interventions;
Explain local, federal and international health policy issues, including the role of agencies (government and non-government) on the development and implementation of health policy;

Recognise individuals who are at risk for under-treatment of their pain (e.g. individuals who are unable to self-report pain, neonates, and cognitively impaired individuals) or populations where care disparities exist;
Identify, critically appraise and apply evidence-based practice to client care;
Communicate appropriately and effectively across written and verbal mediums, with clients, staff, and other health care stakeholders;
Integrate knowledge and skills to effectively plan appropriate client interactions, including client-centred goal development, and the selection of appropriate interventions;
Identify and explain the life-time burden imposed on people with chronic disability and their families;
Propose strategies to facilitate healthcare access for people with chronic disease and disability.
Categorise causes and presentation of intellectual impairment accordingly to major groups and match these to appropriate assessment tools and health services and programs;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Promotional communication (15-20 mins podcast/video recording and a one-page infographic)
Paediatric iSAP case (clinical documentation task; problem list and management plan)

workload_hours: On-campus: You are required to attend and participate in a two-week block of campus-based study that consists of 10 hours of lectures, 12 hours of tutorials , 4 hours of seminars and 8-10 hours of self-directed activity Off-campus clinical placement: You are required to complete a 2-week (or equivalent) clinical placement conducted in a clinical setting focused on disability or chronic disease across the lifespan. This typically comprises the equivalent of 64 hours of clinical placement and 16 hours (or equivalent) of self-directed study in order to complete learning and reflection activities related to your experiences in the delivery of physiotherapy services across the lifespan during this time. Off-campus: When you are not on clinical placement or attending block study days, an average of 14-16 hours of online modules and private study is required weekly.

title: Clinical practice 2
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This clinical placement unit will require you to complete a 5-week full time clinical placement in an acute, subacute/rehabilitation or community setting. This unit will enable you to build upon your knowledge and experience to further develop the competencies required for independent practice as a physiotherapist. Through supervised practice, you will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge and skills in assessment, treatment and client education, whilst working as part of a larger health care team. The professional, ethical and legal aspects of physiotherapy will be applied to practice, providing an opportunity to develop technical, clinical, personal and professional skills. There is a focus on developing skills in feedback dialogue for facilitating learning in self and others. Additional study modules on pharmacology and feedback will supplement the clinical placement experience.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and plan appropriate patient interactions, including patient-centred goal development, and the selection of appropriate interventions;
Critically analyse risks and adverse events associated with client assessments and interventions;
Describe purpose and main methods of qualitative research methods and their use within physiotherapy research.
Describe the steps required for an audit and design a survey for a research question;
Communicate appropriately and effectively across written and verbal mediums, with clients, staff, and other health care stakeholders;
Analyse the ethical principles of conducting clinical-based physiotherapy research;
Tailor knowledge and skills to effectively assess client needs, including selection of relevant measures of health indicators and outcomes;
Identify, critically appraise and apply evidence-based practice to client care;
Reflect critically on practice and propose knowledge and skill gaps and methods to achieve them;
Demonstrate professional behaviour in client care and rights that is culturally sensitive and in accordance with legal requirements;
Analyse the role of feedback in learning;
Synthesise the input of other professions and the patient/ client/family to reach a shared vision of care plans;
Describe and analyse the pharmacological management of common clinical cases;

assessment_tasks.task_name: Assessment of Physiotherapy Practice (5-week clinical placement)

workload_hours: On-campus: Students will have a 2-week on-campus study week. This will include 4 hours of lectures/seminars total. Off-campus clinical placement: You will be allocated 32 contact hours per week for 5 weeks. Variations to placement hours may occur due to public holidays, host organisation factors, or student absences. Make-up placement time may be offered at the discretion of the Department and only when convenient for the organisation in which the placement is taking place. In addition to contact hours, you are expected to complete approximately 8 hours/week of self-directed study related to your clinical placement. Off-campus: During the 7 weeks where you are not on clinical placement, an average of 16 hours of online modules and private study is required weekly.

title: Clinical practice A

syllabus_overview: In this clinical placement unit, you will be required to complete a 5-week full time clinical placement in either an acute, subacute or community setting. This unit will enable you to build upon your knowledge and experience to develop the competencies required for independent practice as a physiotherapist. Through supervised practice, you will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge and skills in assessment, treatment and client education, whilst working as part of a larger health care team. The professional, ethical and legal aspects of physiotherapy will be applied to practice, providing an opportunity to develop technical, clinical, personal and professional skills.
learning_outcomes: Seek, reflect on and respond appropriately to feedback in the practice context.
Deliver person-centred care that is culturally safe, upholds client rights, and is in accordance with legal and ethical standards.
Demonstrate professional behaviour through effective teamwork, reflective practice, and a commitment to ongoing learning.
Critically analyse risks and adverse events associated with physiotherapy practice.
Communicate appropriately and effectively across written and verbal mediums, with clients, staff, and other health care stakeholders.
Tailor knowledge and skills to effectively assess client needs, including selection of relevant measures of health indicators and outcomes.
Analyse, plan and execute appropriate patient interactions, including person-centred goal development and management.
Identify, critically appraise and apply evidence-based practice to person-centred care in physiotherapy.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Assessment of Physiotherapy practice (5 week clinical placement)

workload_hours: A five-week clinical placement, typically comprising 32 hours of clinical placement and approximately 7 hours of self-directed study per week (total of 190 hours in contact and associated work).

title: Clinical essentials A
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this unit, you will continue to build upon your knowledge to further develop the competencies required for independent practice as a physiotherapist. You will reflect on your clinical experience within the Doctor of Physiotherapy so far and integrate it with tutorials and self-directed modules on pharmacology, digital health, dignity during work-integrated learning, appraising clinical guidelines and personal wellbeing.
learning_outcomes: Describe and analyse the pharmacological management of common clinical cases.
Appraise clinical practice guidelines used in physiotherapy practice.
Analyse strategies for the successful management of personal physical and mental wellbeing.
Apply professional, digital and reflective practice skills to support transition to the clinical learning environment.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Clinical practice guideline appraisal (2,400 words equivalent)
Work integrated learning portfolio: personal wellbeing

workload_hours: On-campus: Before your PTY5206 placement, you will complete approximately 7 hours of clinical essentials development delivered as on-campus tutorials. Off-campus: During the 7 weeks when you are not on clinical placement, an average of 16 hours of online modules and private study is required weekly. It is recommended to complete the off-campus workload of this unit in the weeks you are not on clinical placement for PTY5206.

title: Clinical essentials B
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this unit, you will continue to build upon your knowledge to further develop the competencies required for independent practice as a physiotherapist. You will reflect on your clinical experience within the Doctor of Physiotherapy so far and integrate it with tutorials and self-directed modules on qualitative research, clinical audits, survey analysis, health service quality and safety and health service experiences for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
learning_outcomes: Describe the steps required for an audit and design a survey for a research question.
Describe and analyse a client's transition to a new context, referral for further physiotherapy and linkage to relevant clinical and non-clinical support services.
Analyse the impacts of professional culture and the broader health system on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health service experiences.
Analyse the ethical principles of conducting clinical-based physiotherapy research.
Describe the purpose and main methods of qualitative research and apply them to physiotherapy practice contexts.
workload_hours: On-campus: Prior to your PTY5208 placement, you will complete approximately 4 hours of clinical essentials development delivered as live activities. Off-campus: During the 7 weeks when you are not on clinical placement, an average of 16 hours of online modules and private study is required weekly. It is recommended to complete the off-campus workload of this unit in the weeks you are not on clinical placement for PTY5208.

title: Applied research in physiotherapy
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit allows you the opportunity to select and conduct an independent physiotherapy research project over a 12-month period under academic supervision. Building on previous knowledge of ethical research conduct, and exposure to a range of clinical practice challenges in years one and two of the course, you will be supported to define their research question, determine research method, data collection and analysis. Dissemination of research findings will include both an oral and written report. You will will be supported by an academic research supervisor relevant to their area of study for the duration of the research project.
learning_outcomes: Design and develop a clinically relevant research protocol.
Apply evidence-based practice in a range of models of patient care.
Demonstrate and comply with the ethical standards of professional behaviour and communication in the conduct of research.
Communicate research, using appropriate language to extend the knowledge of a range of audiences.
Devise appropriate research methods and collect and record data.
Seek and analyse data to fill student-identified gaps or extend knowledge.
Deliver a verbal presentation and provide constructive peer feedback in an inter-professional seminar setting.
Generate questions/ aims/ hypotheses based on experience, expertise and literature.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Professional conduct - Ethical conduct of research, contribution to peer feedback

workload_hours: On-campus: Fortnightly supervisor/student meetings (one-hour duration) are expected throughout the year, however there is the option for these meetings to be conducted face to face or via video conferencing. Off-campus: This unit is predominantly completed off-campus, although the location of data collection will impact on location of work. title: Clinical practice 3
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This clinical placement unit requires you to complete a 5-week full time clinical placement in an acute, subacute/rehabilitation or community setting. This unit will enable you to build upon your knowledge and experience to further develop the competencies required for independent practice as a physiotherapist. Through supervised practice, you will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge and skills in assessment, treatment and client education, whilst working as part of a larger health care team. The professional, ethical and legal aspects of physiotherapy will be applied to practice, providing an opportunity for you to develop technical, clinical, personal and professional skills. Additional study modules on pain management, delegation and telehealth will supplement the clinical placement experience.
learning_outcomes: Communicate appropriately and effectively across written and verbal mediums, with clients, staff, and other health care stakeholders;
Analyse lifelong strategies to manage physical and mental health, including identifying personal strengths and learning challenges whilst on clinical placements;
Critically analyse risks and adverse events associated with client assessments and interventions;
Reflect critically on practice and propose knowledge and skill gaps and methods to achieve them;
Apply clinical reasoning and diagnostic skill to the interpretation of assessment findings and consequent decision making;
Develop a person-centred, evidence based pain management plan;
Identify, critically appraise and apply evidence-based practice to client care;
Analyse and plan appropriate patient interactions, including patient-centred goal development, and the selection of appropriate interventions;
Demonstrate professional behaviour in client care and rights that is culturally sensitive and in accordance with legal requirements;
Tailor knowledge and skills to effectively assess client needs, including selection of relevant measures of health indicators and outcomes
Describe when and how a client's access to physiotherapy could be improved by resources such as technology;
Recognise when to delegate responsibility to, or accept delegation from, others when it is safe, effective and appropriate;

title: Business and management in health systems
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces you to the business, marketing and management principles required for the successful operation of an allied health business. The concepts of microeconomics and entrepreneurship are introduced and applied to healthcare professionals . The influence and requirements of funding models including private health insurance, Medicare, TAC, Workcover, DVA and NDIS will be analysed with respect to their impact on a business. The clinical and operational governance structures within a range of health care settings will also be compared. This unit will also allow you to consolidate context-specific pre-employment information and processes required for employment including legal and contractual considerations.
learning_outcomes: Explore the importance of market-driven principles to allied health practice.
Apply the business and marketing skills including digital health tools and interventions required for allied health practice.
Critically reflect upon own and observed communication skills required for effective management of others.
Discuss the role of clinical and operational governance in the prevention and minimisation of clinical risks and adverse outcomes.
Differentiate between the models of health funding in allied health including WorkCover, Private Insurance, Chronic Disease Management and NDIS and analyse the impact on practice.
Analyse the ethical considerations and potential conflicts of interest that may confront allied healthcare professionals within business.

title: Leadership, education and advocacy
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: You will develop skills in leadership and advocacy to promote equity, access, and health promotion within allied health and the health and disability sectors more broadly. You will analyse leadership models across a range of different health and advocacy contexts, and examine the role of policy for improving health outcomes for local and global communities. You will also develop and demonstrate skills associated with effective learning and teaching including methods of fostering learning in others. You will develop graduate capabilities related to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and other cultures across the elements of respect, communication, reflection, advocacy, and safety and quality.
learning_outcomes: Apply and analyse critical pre-employment information and processes to support entry into clinical practice.
Describe theories and skills of effective learning and teaching, and apply these to support the learning of other health professionals;
Develop knowledge, skills, and attitudes to collaboratively address racism in healthcare;
Compare and contrast the theories and models of leadership within health;
Analyse a range of public policy issues including equity, equality, and social justice, and propose allied health specific interventions that address these issues;
Integrate advocacy principles to influence policies made by individuals, organisations, and governments at local, national, and international levels;
workload_hours: On-campus: You are required to attend and participate in two blocks of campus-based study that run respectively at the start and end of the semester. This will consist of approximately 15 hours seminars, 5 hours of tutorials, and 10 hours of private study related to seminar and tutorial preparation and revision. Off-campus: To allow for flexibility around placement allocations and other coursework, you will complete the unit content through a combination of synchronous and asynchronous off-campus activities. An average of 8-10 hours of private study is expected over the semester, primarily spent on completing online modules, readings, and working on assessment tasks. An additional 9 hours of online-live tutorials will be scheduled over the semester.

title: Clinical essentials C
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this unit, you will continue to build upon your existing knowledge and skills to further develop the competencies required for safe and effective independent practice as a physiotherapist. You will be encouraged to critically reflect on your clinical experiences to date in the Doctor of Physiotherapy program, identifying areas of strength and opportunities for further development. This reflective process will support the integration of theoretical knowledge with real-world clinical practice. Learning will be supported through self-directed modules focusing on key areas of contemporary physiotherapy practice, including pain management, task delegation, and telehealth. These modules will enable you to deepen your understanding of evidence-based approaches, scope of practice, and models of care, while also developing skills in delivering care across diverse settings and formats.
learning_outcomes: Analyse lifelong strategies to manage physical and mental health, including identifying personal strengths and learning challenges, whilst on clinical placements.
Critically evaluate and justify decisions to delegate responsibility to, or accept delegation from, others when it is safe, effective and appropriate.
Design and justify a person-centred, evidence-informed pain management plan, integrating evidence-based practice, clinical reasoning, and client preferences.
Appraise and recommend strategies to enhance client access to physiotherapy services, including the integration of appropriate technologies and resources to improve equity and outcomes.

Critically reflect on and synthesise clinical practice experiences to identify gaps in knowledge, clinical reasoning, and technical skills, and formulate realistic strategies for professional development.

title: Radiographic science and practice 2
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: RAD1012 develops foundational scientific, professional, and clinical radiographic knowledge essential for you to progress along the Novice to Expert continuum. The unit extends radiographic expertise, enabling safe performance of examinations related to the respiratory system, shoulder and pelvic girdles, vertebral column, bony thorax, and plain abdomen. Building upon earlier principles of professional practice, RAD1012 introduces the science necessary for advanced radiographic equipment operation. You will also study radiation dosimetry and safety, ensuring competent operation and performance measurement of diagnostic ionising radiation equipment. Clinical exposure under supervision allows you to apply these principles across a range of indicated examinations.
learning_outcomes: Summarise the theoretical principles underpinning the operation of automatic exposure control systems and digital radiographic imaging systems.
Apply observation and interviewing skills to provide holistic patient care.
Describe and justify the correct radiographic technique, accounting for clinical presentation, for radiographic imaging of the chest, shoulder and pelvic girdles, the vertebral column, and abdomen.
Describe the statutory regulations governing the safe use of ionising radiation for patient, staff and the public, including dose measurement and monitoring.
Identify when appropriate further and supplementary imaging is required to answer the clinical question.
Define the various quantities of radiation exposure, dose and dose-area product, and perform dosimetric calculations using the correct units.
Recognise the social, cultural and ethical needs encountered in clinical practice.
Apply knowledge and skills to analyse x-ray images and solve imaging challenges associated with patient positioning and image quality.
Apply your knowledge of the impact of x-ray beam properties on image quality factors of an x-ray image.
Explain the biological response of organs to ionising radiation and how to manage the biological risk associated with radiation exposure.
Distinguish between normal radiographic anatomical features and pathological features on x-ray images.
Describe and demonstrate safe radiographic imaging of the chest, shoulder and pelvic girdles, the vertebral column, and abdomen.
prerequisites: RAD1021: Radiologic physics and radiation protection

assessment_tasks.task_name: Clinical learning portfolio (2,000 word equivalent, 5-mins video)

title: Radiologic physics and radiation protection
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit covers the fundamental physics concepts relevant to radiographic imaging. Topics include: Scientific measurement; Mechanics and heat; Atomic structure and electromagnetic radiation; Electricity, magnetism and electromagnetism; X-rays and their production; X-ray emission and interactions between x-rays and matter; Attenuation of x-rays and filters; Detection of X-rays; X-ray image formation; an introduction to computer-based imaging in medicine; and Foundational principles of radiation protection together with statutory requirements.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the fundamental principles of mechanics, electromagnetism and thermal physics relevant to the production and absorption of energy

Use quantitative measures for the absorption of x-rays and discuss why and how x-ray absorption coefficients vary with energy and atomic number and relate these ideas to the sharp depiction of contrast changes in x-ray images of patients;
Explain the effects of ionizing radiation on cellular matter and the basic principles underlying radiation dose and radiation safety
Explain in quantitative terms the production of x-rays and the use of exposure factors that control x-ray intensity, penetration and dose
Explain the physical laws of interaction of particles and waves, including the mechanisms for absorption and scattering of energy at the atomic level
Explain the physical properties of atomic structure

assessment_tasks.task_name: Weekly quizzes (Between 7 and 10 questions-15-20 mins per quiz)

title: Radiologic biology 1
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this unit you will study the anatomy of the upper and lower limbs. You will then apply this knowledge to radiographic appearances of the appendicular skeleton. You will develop an understanding of the complexity of the human body by studying structure and function of cells and tissues. You will also learn how genetic inheritance and biochemical molecules underpin normal biological processes of life. Practicals will reinforce lectures and tutorials.
learning_outcomes: Locate and describe the soft and bony structures that form the lower limb,
Discuss structural and functional features of eukaryotic cells including membrane transport and genetic inheritance,
Locate and describe the soft and bony structures that form the upper limb,
Analyse how different biochemical molecules contribute to cellular metabolism.
Identify and describe the radiographic appearances of the appendicular skeleton and apply this knowledge to radiographic positioning,
Relate the histological characteristics of the 4 tissue types with their respective functions,
prerequisites: RAD1021: Radiologic physics and radiation protection

assessment_tasks.task_name: Teamwork assignment (Equivalent 3,000 words, 10 minute oral presentation)

title: Medical radiation science: Physical principles
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces you to the physical principles underlying imaging modalities which are crucial for both diagnostic and treatment purposes in medical radiation practice. Imaging modalities discussed include radiography, ultrasound, computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging and nuclear medicine imaging. The content covered will include the methods by which each technology produces and enhances the relevant energy forms and how they are accurately measured, processed and recorded to produce a diagnostic image. You will also consider introductory information relating to the design, operation and safety implications of specified instrumentation.
learning_outcomes: Apply the laws of physics, units of measurement and dimensions to solve numerical problems relating to radiation science.
Describe how the interaction of x-rays, gamma rays, sound waves and magnetic fields with matter creates a detectable signal that can be captured to form a diagnostic image.
Explain the design and image formation of imaging modality instrumentation including radiography, CT, Nuclear Medicine, PET, MRI and Ultrasound modalities.
Discuss the safety considerations relating to imaging modality instrumentation and options for managing patient dose.
Reflect on the applications of imaging in the radiation therapy field.
prerequisites: RAD1081: Foundations in medical radiation physics

assessment_tasks.task_name: Quiz series (5 x 20 mins Moodle quizzes)
Laboratory reports (5 x reports, 600 words per report. Total=3,000 words)

workload_hours: 1 hour weekly online lecture, 2 hour weekly contact session (7 weeks are 2-hour-tutorials, 5 weeks are 2-hour-labs across semester), and 2 hours of teacher - directed interaction with Moodle-based tasks per week. You will be expected to engage in additional self-directed activities to facilitate the development of knowledge and understanding of the physical concepts covered in the unit for 7 hours each week. You will be expected to engage in additional self-directed readings to facilitate the development of knowledge and understanding of the physical concepts covered in the unit.

title: Foundations in medical radiation physics
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to provide you with the opportunity to develop theoretical knowledge in the concepts underpinning medical radiation physics. The unit begins with an examination of mathematical principles related to medical radiation physics. You will then study the laws of physics, the units of measurement used within the discipline, electricity, magnetism and the electromagnetic spectrum. You will learn about the physical properties of atomic structure and about the interaction of particles and waves including mechanisms for absorption and scattering of energy at the atomic level. The focus will then move to the properties of radiation, radiation interactions with matter, and the production and detection of radiation. Foundation principles of radiation safety and radiation protection together with statutory requirements will be covered. The physics concepts discussed will be applied in a radiation therapy context in relation to principles, implications and instrumentation.
learning_outcomes: Describe the effects of ionising radiation on cellular matter.
Examine the principles of radiation safety and radiation protection that apply to the use of medical radiations.
Explain the principles and properties of atomic structure, radioactivity, the processes of radiation interactions with matter and the production, absorption and scattering of energy.
Describe the instrumentation used for the production of x-rays including the Diagnostic X-ray Tube and the Medical Linear Accelerator.
Analyse laboratory findings and communicate these in written form.
Describe fundamental mathematics and physics concepts relevant to medical radiation physics, focussing on mechanics, waves and particles, thermal physics, electricity, magnetism and electromagnetism.
Discuss the principles of radiation detection and dosimetry relevant to medical radiation physics.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Laboratory reports (750 words each report. Total 3,000 words)
Quiz series (5 x 20 mins. Moodle Quizzes; MCQs/SAQs/EMQs and open-ended)

workload_hours: 1 hour online lecture, 2 hour weekly contact session (7 weeks are 2-hour-tutorials, 5 weeks are 2-hour-labs across semester), and 2 hours of teacher - directed interaction with Moodle based tasks per week. You will be expected to engage in additional self-directed activities to facilitate the development of knowledge and understanding of the physical concepts covered in the unit for 7 hours each week.

title: Radiographic science and practice 1
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit delivers the initial scientific, professional and clinical radiographic knowledge that will be foundational in subsequent Radiographic Science and Practice units as you progresses along the Novice to Expert continuum of development. The unit introduces you to the requisite knowledge required to perform radiographic examinations of the limbs and chest and the fundamentals of professional practice to include the behavioural sciences, communication and legally and ethically correct working practices. Clinical exposure to patients under supervision will enable you to apply these principles across the range of examinations indicated.
learning_outcomes: Under supervision safely conduct radiographic examinations of the elbow, forearm, wrist, hand, fingers and thumb, knee, tibia and fibula, ankle, calcaneum, foot, toes and chest of an adult ambulant patient;

Record and obtain information from individuals employing appropriate observation and interviewing skills, such that the information generated may be integrated with basic scientific theory and knowledge to provide quality levels of patient care;
Recognise and adapt, in a professional manner, to the variety of social, cultural and ethical perspectives that may legitimately be encountered within clinical practice;

Describe and justify the radiographic projections, body positions and the radiographic exposure factors underpinning general radiographic examinations of the elbow, forearm, wrist, hand, fingers and thumb, knee, tibia and fibula, ankle, calcaneum, foot, toes and chest of an adult ambulant patient;

Describe and apply within a professional standards and ethics context theories of the psychosocial impact on human behaviour, communication and occupational health and safety of the working environment;
Distinguish anatomical features on radiographic images and recognise common radiologic pathologies or traumatic appearances in terms of the clinical question being asked;

Evaluate the radiographic request form, obtain a clinical history from a patient, select appropriate radiographic protocols consisting of radiographic projections positioning techniques and exposure factors to produce high quality projection(s) that will aid the diagnostic process;
Evaluate radiographs in terms of technical quality and positioning criteria and where necessary devise appropriate problem-solving strategies for less than optimal radiographic projections;

Position an adult patient, accounting for his/her clinical presentation, for the radiographic projections identified in the protocol, direct and align the central ray to an appropriate bony landmark and image receptor.
In the light of the clinical problem, assess the appropriateness of supplementary projections, and where required position the patient for the required further images;
prerequisites: RAD1021: Radiologic physics and radiation protection

assessment_tasks.task_name: Clinical learning portfolio (2,000 words equivalent and 5 minute video)

workload_hours: 3 x one hour lectures, 2 x one hour tutorials, 1 x two hour laboratory practical session, 3 hours clinical practice per week.

title: Radiologic biology 2
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: You will continue your anatomy study starting with the soft and bony structures of the vertebral column, followed by the thorax and thoracic contents. The early stages of embryo development are explored. You will be introduced to the principles of pathology, and will then apply this knowledge to the respiratory and musculoskeletal systems. Study of physiology of these systems will underpin your understanding of pathological processes. You will learn to identify normal and abnormal radiographic anatomy on plain film radiographs in regions of the limbs, spine, thorax and abdomen.
learning_outcomes: Identify normal and abnormal anatomy on radiographic images of the vertebral column & thorax abdomen and musculoskeletal system
Describe the basic physiology of the musculoskeletal, respiratory, cardiovascular and nervous system;
Evaluate the effect of environment and nutrition on the health of an individual or community;
Identify fundamental principles of pathology and apply this knowledge to specific cases, in particular the musculoskeletal and respiratory systems;
Describe the anatomy of the vertebral column, spinal cord and thoracic cage and thoracic contents;
List major stages that occur in embryology and extrapolate how congenital abnormalities can occur
prerequisites: RAD1021: Radiologic physics and radiation protection
workload_hours: This unit has equivalent of 6 hours of directed study per week (averaged over 12 week Semester). This includes a mix of teaching and learning activities such as lectures, workshops, tutorials, practical activities The workload is approximately: 4 lectures/wk 1 x 2hr Rad Imaging tutorials/wk 1 x 2hr Pathology workshops/wk 5 x 2hr Anatomy practicals / semester Self-directed study includes reading/listening to lectures, reading recommended texts, completing activities & practical workbooks and practice quizzes

title: Medical imaging science: Radiographic principles
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit is designed to provide you with the requisite knowledge and understanding of the scientific and technological principles associated with the practice of diagnostic radiography. You will be introduced to radiographic terminology, image critique and analysis with a particular emphasis on the axial skeleton and musculoskeletal system, the thorax, abdomen and pelvis. An introduction to the design of the modern radiologic suite and the role of medical imaging in radiation therapy will be provided. In addition, an overview of the production of the X-ray image and the safety features related to the use of radiation in a radiographic environment will be studied.
learning_outcomes: Describe radiographic positioning skills and protocols to produce images of the thorax, abdomen and pelvis.
Employ radiographic positioning skills and protocols to produce images of a representative section of the axial skeleton and musculoskeletal system.
Identify the key features of the use of radiation, how it produces the image, and its safe use in diagnostic radiographic practice.
Distinguish the anatomical features and recognise associated common radiographic pathologies of the axial skeleton and musculoskeletal system, the thorax, abdomen and pelvis.
Describe the general characteristics of the modern X-ray system used in clinical practice, including scientific principles, and production of the digital image.
prerequisites: RAD1022: Medical radiation science: Physical principles

assessment_tasks.task_name: In semester Moodle tests (2 x 20 mins)

workload_hours: 1 hour lecture per week 2 hour tutorial per week 6 hours self-directed activities and study per week

title: Medical imaging anatomy
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: You will build upon first year foundational knowledge of human anatomy and apply this knowledge across a range of planar radiographic images. You will learn how to identify and recognise normal radiographic appearances of important structures as represented on digital radiographic images. You will also be introduced to different imaging modalities, and learn how to recognise the anatomical representation and relationship of important body structures in multiple imaging planes.
learning_outcomes: Describe and differentiate the magnetic resonance radiographic representation of commonly performed MRI regions: magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP), brain & spine.
Differentiate between the bony and soft tissue elements and joints which comprise the upper and lower limbs on digital planar radiographic and computed tomography images.
Name and identify the primary anatomical structures of the head, neck and spine as represented on computed tomography images.

Describe and differentiate the basic computed tomography radiographic representation of the primary organs comprising cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, urinary, & reproductive systems both with and without contrast enhancement
Discriminate between the osseous, soft tissue components and primary muscles of the shoulder, hip, knee & spine on MR images.
Name and identify the anatomical and soft tissue structures represented on digital planar radiographic images
prerequisites: BMA1011: Foundations of anatomy and physiology for health practice 1
BMA1012: Foundations of anatomy and physiology for health practice 2
workload_hours: 1 hour lecture, 2 hour tutorial per week, 3 hours of teacher - directed interaction with Moodle based tasks per week. You will be expected to engage in an additional 6 hours of self-directed learning to facilitate the appropriate level of knowledge of the topics covered in the unit.

title: Medical imaging science: Nuclear medicine
school: Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences
syllabus_overview: This unit is designed to provide you with the requisite knowledge and understanding of the scientific and technological principles associated with the practice underpinning Nuclear Medicine. You will explore the topics of radiopharmacy, nuclear medicine physics and instrumentation techniques and procedures and care of the patient in the nuclear medicine department. You will also be introduced to the role of hybrid imaging in medical radiation practice.
learning_outcomes: Describe and explain physical principles and instrumentation used in nuclear medicine in the context of image acquisition, quality control and radiopharmaceutical administration techniques
Describe basic principles of radiation protection with regard to the use of unsealed sources justifying the need for a regulatory framework governing their use
Identify patient contra-indications to nuclear medicine procedures
Evaluate the usefulness of nuclear medicine procedures/techniques in the context of specific patient diagnoses and communicate these findings to their peers
Explain the characteristics of radiopharmaceuticals used diagnostic imaging and for therapeutic purposes;
Describe hybrid imaging and discuss its application and advantages in medical radiation practice
prerequisites: RAD1022: Medical radiation science: Physical principles
